criteria: GuestNetworkExecWiring::new(clock) / gate() / supervisor() construct one private mutex/Notify state that starts BootClosed with no recovery snapshot; GuestNetworkExecGate, GuestNetworkExecSupervisor, and GuestNetworkExecClaim are each private-field, non-`Clone` types whose only cloneable handle is their own `Arc`, and none is constructible outside GuestNetworkExecWiring.

GuestNetworkExecGate::claim_release returns one opaque claim lifetime only from Open; from BootClosed or Recovering it registers a Notify waiter before unlocking and retries after wake without touching VM pending-EXEC state; from FailStop it returns None immediately; GuestNetworkExecClaim's Drop ends that lifetime under the same lock and wakes waiters. Private active-claim counter bookkeeping is not an independently observed outcome.

GuestNetworkExecSupervisor::open_after_boot performs only BootClosed -> Open, wakes waiters, and returns false from every other state; is_boot_closed is the read-only precondition check used immediately before fresh-process mutation and is never treated as a runtime health signal; begin_recovery performs only Open -> Recovering and returns true only for the winning transition; complete_attempt applies only while Recovering, updates the first-remaining component or transitions to Open and wakes waiters, and returns false after Open/FailStop so late work cannot overwrite either; recovery_progress returns a value snapshot only while Recovering and None in every other state; fail_stop atomically transitions BootClosed/Open/Recovering -> FailStop, returns the one request to send on its first call and None on every later call (first-request-wins, idempotent-send), and wakes waiters. (This enumeration of GuestNetworkExecSupervisor's surface is non-exhaustive -- see feature-delta.md for the complete method list.)

release_for_exit_emission acquires a gate claim strictly before it reads pending_exec or gate_sender; an Open claim is held through the beacon-writer acknowledgement; a Recovering caller waits without taking either value and proceeds only once recovery reopens the gate; a FailStop caller is woken with None so EXEC is never taken or written and process shutdown owns the remaining VMM/gate teardown; an already-written command is never paused or frozen.

steps.description: Activate the native-metal walking-skeleton body proving two checked-in VM workloads communicate by name through real overdrive serve + overdrive deploy <SPEC>, encrypted on the peer wire (TLS 1.3, kTLS TX/RX, splice, zero cleartext), on the direct-host-TAP shared-bridge topology with no per-workload netns/veth/slot, and owned total cleanup. criteria: The callee VM Service reports Running with replicas 1/1 and the caller VM Job reports success dependent on receiving the callee's reply, driven entirely through the real overdrive serve + overdrive deploy <SPEC> production entry points -- no test-only wiring installs a rule, binds a socket, programs a map, or supplies an address that production does not install/bind/program/supply itself.

For this same-node peer, the authoritative peer-facing byte boundary is the exact leg-B/leg-C TCP segment on loopback after the nft output divert and fwmark/table-100 local route, before leg-C decryption -- never the shared bridge. A loss-accounted AF_PACKET capture bound to the exact lo ifindex before caller-VMM release must uniquely correlate one live `ss -H -n -t -i -e` leg-B tuple from the shared-bridge gateway address to the ServiceBackendsResolve-selected workload address and declared port; one record must contain tcp-ulp-tls, TLS 1.3, txconf, and rxconf; that tuple and exact reverse must each reassemble at least one application_data record (0x17) and contain zero hits for either byte-distinct plaintext marker. The same live ss inode must map through /proc/self/fd to one in-process leg-B fd, and the existing strace-style thread-group observation must show completed positive splice(2) calls with that fd as destination for the post-establishment request and source for its response, followed by the byte-exact guest reply. Zero/multiple tuple or inode/fd matches, a missing direction, capture drop/truncation/gap/conflict, a non-loopback exact-tuple frame, or splice on another socket fails closed; all-interface capture is diagnostic only and no product/test-hook API may be added.

A separate loss-accounted shared-bridge/TAP capture proves the intentional guest-local plaintext boundaries: the caller guest-address-to-frontend flow toward leg F and both byte-distinct markers on exactly one non-kTLS leg-S tuple from node gateway address and ephemeral port to Service workload address and declared port, plus its reverse after leg-C decryption, while proving no direct caller-guest-to-Service-guest bypass. That plaintext capture cannot satisfy the loopback TLS oracle. The same topology evidence shows both VMs attached directly to the node-local shared bridge via TAP with no per-workload network namespace, veth pair, transit/guest /30, NetSlot, or host_veth anywhere on the production path; cross-host physical-wire evidence is outside #295.
